speakers.name: Salmaan Allibhai
speakers.title: Chief Actuary and head of data and analytics

exchanges.question: Can you quantify how the newly disclosed new business quotes and bind orders have trended year over year and quarter over quarter, and how should that KPI be viewed relative to submission growth? Second, given the expense ratio advantage and best-in-class returns, is Kinsale willing to let the accident year loss ratio deteriorate for higher near-term growth?
exchanges.answer: Kehoe said the more granular disclosure was added at investor request, but more granular numbers are more volatile and one should not overthink 90-day moves; across the 25 divisions the picture is a competitive market overall with plenty of opportunity in some places and slower growth in others. On trading loss ratio for growth, he said all product lines are managed to a low 20s return on equity or greater with pricing constantly adjusted in both directions, and with ROE at 24% for the quarter he would not expect a meaningful deterioration from that.

exchanges.question: Was there anything one-off, such as favorable non-cat weather, in the better-than-expected accident year loss ratio (up 40 basis points year over year), and how should it move from here given mix shift toward casualty? Second, why did E&S Homeowners decline 22% in the quarter, and how is Kinsale thinking about reinsurance retentions at the upcoming renewal given a below-average hurricane forecast and lower reinsurance cost?
exchanges.responderTitle: Chief Actuary and head of data and analytics
exchanges.answer: Allibhai said there was nothing out of the ordinary and no one-time adjustments, noting only that the current accident year loss ratio has some seasonality with the first quarter typically a little higher than other quarters. Winston said the high-value homeowners market is seeing increased competition and Kinsale is offering lower limits so average premium is dropping, while the Personal Insurance division, also a homeowners book, is still showing good growth. Kehoe said retentions and limits are reviewed every year and have been increased many times over 17 years, they will look again this year, he cannot commit to how the treaties will be placed, and the renewal date is 6/1.

exchanges.question: How has competitive behavior in casualty changed over the past six months, whether from MGAs or admitted carriers, and where has it been more stable than expected? Second, how much of the slowdown in submission growth versus a year ago is demand-driven versus a pullback from irrational pricing, and what initiatives are under way to expand broker relationships or penetration?
exchanges.answer: Kehoe said the market is competitive and division-level growth rates are a proxy for competitiveness. Winston said there is a lot of competition from fronts, MGAs and new companies on long-tail lines, specifically construction, over the last four-five months, revving up aggressively, while premises liability is still strong and anything auto-related offers meaningful opportunities; Kehoe added that larger transactions are a different market and small to medium-size accounts are a safe harbor. On submissions, Kehoe said they are an imperfect leading indicator, ex-commercial property submissions up 9% is an attractive rate, the market is competitive but reasonably steady, and stress on larger accounts depresses growth only until those accounts transition off the books and growth normalizes; Kinsale is principally a wholesale model, always looks for top quality brokers and supports experienced broker teams starting new shops.

exchanges.question: Is there any change in retention, or is the gap between gross premium and submission growth mostly pricing, exposure and the mix impact from large commercial property? Second, larger competitors say technology may let them compete for smaller customers in small business E&S and admitted; is there evidence of that emerging?
exchanges.answer: Winston said new business and renewal hit ratios have been consistent quarter to quarter for a long time with no big change. Kehoe said no, technology has been a core competency since the company started 17 years ago, the expense ratio is partly a proxy for Kinsale's technology lead, and the company can adopt new software, hardware and AI models faster because of its tech professionals and the absence of legacy software going back 20, 30, 40 years; competitors would have to speak to their own positions.

exchanges.question: On property, has competition and pricing reset at a lower level that is now being run through until easier comps, or is it still drifting down? Second, has the expense advantage already been deployed to the appropriate degree, or will it be used further to push top-line growth? Third, how is the equity portfolio performing?
exchanges.answer: Kehoe said there is no good news to report on property and, as last year, easier comps come in the second half of the year because a disproportionate share of commercial property volume is written in the first six months. On the expense advantage, he said the company constantly estimates loss costs across short, medium and long-tail lines, combines its expense, underwriting and analytics advantages with conservative reserving backed by a 17-year track record of favorable development, is ambitious to grow but subordinates growth to profitability, and the 0.5% GWP decline reflects the book shifting to smaller average premiums with top-notch profitability. The equity portfolio is about 2/3 actively managed and 1/3 passive, principally S&P 500; it has lagged the S&P since late 2022 but more or less matched its benchmark, the Vanguard VYM high-dividend ETF, due to a lower tech weighting and value orientation.

exchanges.question: Of the commercial property division premium, $65 million in the first quarter versus $375 million last year, what portion is actually the large property category facing competition? Second, with capital entering the space at lower return targets, will the market normalize back to Kinsale's low 20s ROE target or might it need to come down to the high teens long term?
exchanges.answer: Kehoe said there is no specific breakout but average premium in that division is somewhere between $30,000-$40,000 per policy, down from north of $50,000 a year or two ago, reflecting lost larger accounts or participating higher in the schedule with less risk, and a trend toward smaller accounts. Winston clarified that the commercial property division is the standalone large shared and layered division, with small property broken out separately. On ROE, Kehoe said no, they are confident in a low 20s return on equity given a better underwriting model and a significant cost advantage, viewing it as roughly 15 percentage points of spread over a risk-free rate (10-year treasury) a little below 5%.

exchanges.question: How does Kinsale's submission growth rate compare to the overall market or the E&S sub-segment where it competes, to gauge where the macro is trending and how Kinsale is running against it?
exchanges.answer: Kehoe said they have no specific information on the overall market. Brokers canvass the market to get low cost and broad coverage for clients, so he assumes some commonality between Kinsale's stats and competitors', but they do not really know.

exchanges.question: With more competition in construction, has there been any slowdown or delay in construction activity? Second, how did general casualty growth (11% or 12%, double digits) compare sequentially to the fourth quarter after low 20s growth last year? Third, will cash from operations (up 8%) track net written premium, and what guideposts matter for free cash flow this year?
exchanges.answer: Winston said they have not seen delays, though Kinsale mostly does not write large project-specific policies; some projects are being delayed out west and in the northeast for wraps, which is not where the construction book is focused. Kehoe said they do not have sequential general casualty stats to provide today but the 10-K has gross written premium by underwriting division with a three-year look back. Petrucelli said trending cash from operations with net written premium is a good way to look at it.
